thesis_statement: Viral Entry Mechanism Axiom: Viral surface glycoproteins must structurally bind to specific host cell receptors to mediate membrane fusion
parent_thesis: Thermodynamic Protein Folding Axiom: Amino acid sequences autonomously fold into the lowest-energy 3D conformations (Anfinsen's dogma)
formal_proof: Viral entry requires a high-affinity protein-protein interaction. A viral ligand (L) binds to a cellular receptor (R) forming complex (LR) if the dissociation constant Kd = [L][R]/[LR] is sufficiently low, which is determined strictly by the complementary folded structures of both proteins.
context_description: Viruses can only infect a cell if their outer proteins act as a perfect physical 'key' to the cell's 'lock'. This relies entirely on how those proteins folded into their 3D shapes.
